{{Short description|Derivative in differential geometry and vector calculus}}
{{see also|Exterior covariant derivative}}
In the math branches of [[differential geometry]] and [[vector calculus]], the '''second [[covariant derivative]]''', or the '''second order covariant derivative''', of a vector field is the derivative of its derivative with respect to another two [[tangent vector]] fields.

==Definition==
Formally, given a (pseudo)-Riemannian [[manifold]] (''M'', ''g'') associated with a [[vector bundle]] ''E'' → ''M'', let ∇ denote the [[Levi-Civita connection]] given by the metric ''g'', and denote by Γ(''E'') the space of the [[smoothness|smooth]] [[Section (fiber bundle)|sections]] of the total space ''E''. Denote by ''T<sup>*</sup>M'' the [[cotangent bundle]] of ''M''. Then the second covariant derivative can be defined as the [[function composition|composition]] of the two ∇s as follows: <ref>{{cite web|last1=Parker|first1=Thomas H.|title=Geometry Primer|url=http://www.math.msu.edu/~parker/ga/geometryprimer.pdf|accessdate=2 January 2015}}, pp. 7</ref>
:<math>\Gamma(E) \stackrel{\nabla}{\longrightarrow} \Gamma(T^*M \otimes E) \stackrel{\nabla}{\longrightarrow} \Gamma(T^*M \otimes T^*M \otimes E).</math>
For example, given vector fields ''u'', ''v'', ''w'', a second [[covariant derivative]] can be written as
:<math>(\nabla^2_{u,v} w)^a = u^c v^b \nabla_c \nabla_b w^a</math>
by using [[abstract index notation]]. It is also straightforward to verify that
:<math>(\nabla_u \nabla_v w)^a = u^c \nabla_c v^b \nabla_b w^a = u^c v^b \nabla_c \nabla_b w^a + (u^c \nabla_c v^b) \nabla_b w^a = (\nabla^2_{u,v} w)^a + (\nabla_{\nabla_u v} w)^a.</math>
Thus
:<math>\nabla^2_{u,v} w = \nabla_u \nabla_v w - \nabla_{\nabla_u v} w.</math>
When the [[torsion tensor]] is zero, so that <math>[u,v]= \nabla_uv-\nabla_vu</math>, we   may use this fact to write [[Riemann curvature tensor]] as  <ref>{{cite web|author=[[Jean Gallier]] and Dan Guralnik|title=Chapter 13: Curvature in Riemannian Manifolds|url=http://www.cis.upenn.edu/~cis610/diffgeom5.pdf|accessdate=2 January 2015}}</ref>
:<math>R(u,v) w=\nabla^2_{u,v} w - \nabla^2_{v,u} w.</math>
Similarly, one may also obtain the second covariant derivative of a function ''f'' as
:<math>\nabla^2_{u,v} f = u^c v^b \nabla_c \nabla_b f = \nabla_u \nabla_v f - \nabla_{\nabla_u v} f.</math>
Again, for the  torsion-free    Levi-Civita connection, and   for any vector fields ''u'' and ''v'', when we  feed the function ''f'' into  both sides of 
:<math>\nabla_u v - \nabla_v u = [u, v]</math>
we  find 
:<math>(\nabla_u v - \nabla_v u)(f) = [u, v](f) = u(v(f)) - v(u(f)).</math>.
This can be rewritten as 
:<math>\nabla_{\nabla_u v} f - \nabla_{\nabla_v u} f = \nabla_u \nabla_v f - \nabla_v \nabla_u f,</math>
so we have 
:<math>\nabla^2_{u,v} f = \nabla^2_{v,u} f.</math>
That is, the value of the second covariant derivative of a function is independent on the order of taking derivatives.
